Alex — attaching a compact implementation checklist to make the CS→Eng handoff explicit (attached: CS-Implementation-Checklist.xlsx). High level asks before we schedule the infra handoff call:

1) SSO/SAML: please confirm the SAML metadata file and assertion attributes you want for email/uid (I attached saml-metadata-Globex.xml that our engineer expects).
2) SCIM: we need a final attribute mapping and the expected provisioning cadence (realtime vs nightly). I attached SCIM-schema-v2.json as our baseline.
3) IP allowlist: list of public egress ranges for your cluster(s) and whether we should support a CIDR prefix or single-IP NAT.
4) Service accounts: name convention and whether you require short-lived keys / KMS integration.
5) Org policies: any tenant-level restrictions (e.g., prohibited roles, MFA enforcement) that should be enforced at provisioning time.

Proposed MAP:
- Aug 28: confirm metadata + IP ranges (you)
- Aug 30: engineering intake + templated terraform for allowlist (our infra)
- Sep 3: test provisioning on staging with SCIM (both sides)
- Sep 10: canary live cutover window

If you can confirm SAML metadata and IP CIDRs today, I’ll loop in Rishi (security) and schedule the engineering intake.

Attachments: CS-Implementation-Checklist.xlsx, saml-metadata-Globex.xml, SCIM-schema-v2.json

Ben — thanks, this is helpful. A few quick notes from our side:

- SAML: attaching our current metadata fragment (partial) in the thread. We use EmailAddress and UPN as assertion attributes. Can you confirm Redwood requires a NameID format?
- SCIM: we do prefer realtime provisioning (SCIM push) for user create/deactivate. The mapping we need: email -> userName, displayName -> name.formatted, groups -> groups.value.
- IP allowlist: our security team prefers using a small set of fixed NAT egress IPs per region. For testing, we can provide the staging NATs (10.14.2.0/30, 10.14.2.4/30) and prod will be different — I’ll send prod ranges after procurement.
- Service accounts: we use a convention: svc-redwood-<env>-<purpose> and require HSM-backed key storage for production. Short-lived tokens (1h) are preferred.

Two asks: can Rishi confirm whether Redwood supports SCIM bulk fixes (we will occasionally sync 1000 users at once), and can you share a sample provisioning log format for our audit team?

I’m looping in procurement (cc). We can target the MAP dates but will need procurement sign-off before prod ranges are shared.

Alex/Team — quick security clarifications after reviewing the fragments Ben shared:

- NameID: we support EmailAddress and transient NameID; for SAML assertions we recommend persistent NameID using email to simplify account linking. If you require UPN we can map it but will need explicit mapping rules.
- SCIM: Redwood supports both incremental and bulk SCIM PATCH/POST. For large one-time bulk fixes we recommend using our bulk endpoint (rate-limited) during an agreed maintenance window — provide an estimate of the peak sync size and we’ll provision temporary throughput.
- IP allowlist: we cannot depend on RFC1918 private ranges (10.x) for production egress — those must be translated to public NAT IPs. For staging the private ranges you gave are fine; for prod please share the public egress CIDRs.
- Service accounts / keys: we will accept HSM-backed keys (KMS integration) for production. For service account naming, please follow the svc-redwood-<env>-<purpose> pattern and include a short description in the account metadata. We recommend short-lived tokens (TTL 1h) and rotating credentials; we can integrate with your KMS if needed.
